chunks: “Indeed, Banī Taghlib refused the jizyah and asked ʿUmar to exempt them. So he feared that they would join the Romans, and he made a settlement with them on the basis that he would remove that from their heads and double the charity upon them. They accepted that, so upon them is what they made settlement upon and were content with, until the truth appears.”

key_terms.الرُّومِ: the Romans, whom ʿUmar feared they might join
key_terms.الصَّدَقَةَ: charity, here referring to the financial payment imposed on them
key_terms.الْجِزْيَةِ: jizyah, the levy they refused to pay
key_terms.الْحَقُّ: the truth, whose appearance marks the end point mentioned in the report
key_terms.بَنِي تَغْلِبَ: Banī Taghlib, the tribe being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.رُءُوسِهِمْ: their heads, meaning the per-person liability was removed from them
key_terms.صَالَحَهُمْ: he made a settlement with them

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha عليه السلام say about Banī Taghlib and their agreement regarding jizyah and charity?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a political and financial settlement made with Banī Taghlib when they refused to pay jizyah. Imam al-Ridha عليه السلام states that they remain bound by the terms they accepted until the truth becomes manifest.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1611 - Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (as) said:

"The Banu Taghlib were reluctant to pay the Jizyah and requested Umar to exempt them. Fearing that they might join the Romans, he made a treaty with them, whereby the Jizyah was removed from their heads, and instead, their charity (Zakat) was doubled. They accepted this arrangement. Thus, they are bound by what they agreed to and accepted until the truth prevails (the rule of justice is established)."
